title: Open Zaak holds the zaak in a mutable API, so municipal audit has no history the case system cannot rewrite
content:
Open Zaak is the Common Ground component that holds the zaak — the case — and it exposes it through an API that carries its current state, status included. Status changes are writes against that API, and the account of them lives in the same store that performs them.

The requirement the research names is independence. Dutch municipal audit needs a replayable history of status changes that the case system itself cannot rewrite. When the record and the system producing it are the same store, the audit rests on the trustworthiness of the thing being audited, which is a structural problem rather than a configuration one — more logging inside the case system does not resolve it.

Maykin's position as a Common Ground implementer means the gap sits at a shared interface rather than in bespoke code. Status transitions look the same across municipalities, so the dispatch point is predictable: one interface, many tenants. That is what makes this fit reusable instead of a single engagement.
